findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a post-rollback assertion to the plan stating what consumers see after reverting code on a ticket whose SNAPSHOT contains `file_impact_scope: 'none'` (e.g. 'rolled-back readers treat the ticket as undeclared; document this as a compensating-forward scenario and note that the stored bytes are preserved for re-deploy recovery').
evidence: process_snapshot restores compiled_state verbatim: 'for key, value in compiled_state.items(): state[key] = value' — unknown keys from a rolled-back deployment are simply ignored by old code
ticket_state.schema.json has `"additionalProperties": true`, so old readers won't error, but will silently treat scope as undeclared
Plan states no rollback / back-out path for the new persisted state keys
ABSENCE: no plan text addresses what rolled-back consumers see after a SNAPSHOT baked with the new keys
findings.finding: The plan does not assert on the post-rollback semantic state of tickets whose SNAPSHOT has been compacted with `file_impact_scope: 'none'`. On rollback, the SNAPSHOT JSON retains the key bytes-intact, but rolled-back code ignores the unknown key and treats the ticket as `undeclared` (empty `file_impact` + no recognised scope). The explicit 'no file impact' declaration is silently lost to rolled-back readers without any warning or compensating-forward path stated in the plan.
findings.location: Approach section / Scope: `src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py` (process_snapshot) / post-rollback schema state
scenarios: Team deploys this story, an operator runs `rebar set-file-impact <id> --none '...'`, the ticket is compacted (SNAPSHOT written with file_impact_scope='none'), then the story is rolled back. All consumers now silently treat the ticket as 'undeclared', potentially triggering conservative downstream behaviour (e.g. S2/S3/S4/S5 gates that treat undeclared differently from none).
A partially-completed deploy where some workers run new code (write scope='none') and others run old code (read, ignore the key) diverges silently.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a brief rollback note to the Approach section: 'A SNAPSHOT written with file_impact_scope="none" is preserved byte-for-byte on rollback; rolled-back code ignores the key and treats the ticket as undeclared. This is a read-time semantic regression, not data loss — re-deploying the story restores correct behaviour. Operators who need immediate rollback correctness should re-run set-file-impact after rollback to record a zero-length array explicitly.'
